home.interludeTitle: Somewhere between the jungle and the sea.
home.interludeBody: Las Terrenas sits on the north coast of the Samaná Peninsula — a place that somehow missed the resort development that overtook the rest of the island. The beaches are long and uncrowded. The town is small and European in character. The peninsula is covered in jungle right up to the water's edge.
home.escapeTitle: A private corner of the Caribbean.
home.escapeBody: La Dolce Vita is a two-bedroom, air-conditioned apartment that sleeps 4–6 guests, in a quiet residential complex five minutes from the beach. Private pool, full kitchen, outdoor terrace. Designed for people who travel to actually be somewhere.

about.intro1: A private two-bedroom residence on the Samaná Peninsula, steps from one of the most beautiful beaches in the Dominican Republic. The apartment sits on Ave 27 de Febrero in Las Terrenas — a town that feels like the south of France dropped into the Caribbean.
about.intro2: Two air-conditioned bedrooms, two private bathrooms, a full kitchen, and a private pool shaded by palms. Sleeps 4–6 guests comfortably. Quiet enough for two. The kind of place where a week turns into a longer conversation.
about.address: Ave 27 de Febrero, Apartment 2 · Las Terrenas, Samaná · Dominican Republic
areaFacts: French and Italian expat community — cosmopolitan but Caribbean-relaxed.
Three languages on the street: Dominican Spanish, French, and English.
Food truck park in town, open daily from 4 pm with twelve trucks.
Nearest airport: Samaná El Catey (AZS). Santo Domingo (SDQ) is two hours by road.
Best weather: December through May. Whale watching season January through March.

beaches.name: Playa Punta Popy
beaches.body: The closest beach to the residence. The town beach — calm clear water, a boardwalk lined with cafés and beach bars, and a lively atmosphere most evenings. Good for a morning coffee with your feet in the sand, or a long afternoon with nowhere to be.

beaches.name: Playa Bonita
beaches.body: Widely considered the most beautiful beach in Las Terrenas. Calm turquoise water, white sand, and palm trees that lean into the wind. Boutique hotels and restaurants along the shore. The sunsets here are unhurried and spectacular — the kind that make you stay longer than planned.

beaches.name: Playa Las Ballenas
beaches.body: Quiet and windswept, with an end-of-the-world feeling that the other beaches lack. Best walked at golden hour, when the light turns amber and the beach is mostly empty.

beaches.name: Playa Cosón
beaches.body: Seven kilometres of wild, undeveloped beach — one of the longest in the Dominican Republic. A favourite among surfers and anyone who wants to feel genuinely far from civilisation. Bring water.

beaches.name: Playa Morón
beaches.body: Remote and peaceful, with almost no crowds even in high season. Pristine water, dramatic cliffs nearby, and the kind of silence that's hard to find anywhere on the peninsula.

beaches.name: Playa Rincón
beaches.body: Consistently ranked among the best beaches in the Caribbean — and it earns it. A long arc of white sand backed by coconut palms, with a river at one end and clear Atlantic water. Worth every minute of the drive.

beaches.name: Cayo Levantado
beaches.body: A small island in Samaná Bay — also known as Bacardi Island after a commercial filmed here in the 1970s. Voted one of the world's top 50 beaches. White sand, palm trees leaning over the water, and turquoise you can see straight through to the bottom. Only reachable by ferry from Samaná town.

beaches.name: Las Galeras
beaches.body: A small fishing village at the far tip of the Samaná Peninsula. The drive alone is worth it — winding roads through jungle and hills. Several small beaches within the village, each one more secluded than the last.
